equations.section: III.A Retained distinction and graph structure
equations.text: delta_R = (a # b);  delta_R => L_R = D_W - W;  S_{n+1} = F(S_n, u_n, c_n, T_n)
equations.meaning: States the root weld of Readout Genesis: a retained distinction forces a weighted-graph Laplacian form, and the root state evolves through a context-sensitive stepper.

equations.section: III.A Retained distinction and graph structure
equations.text: q_{D,n+1} o F_n = F^#_{D,n} o q_{D,n};  O_{D,n} = O^#_{D,n} o q_{D,n}
equations.meaning: An admissible domain translation must commute with the root dynamics and the root readout operator.

equations.section: III.A Retained distinction and graph structure
equations.text: delta_R = (a # b)
equations.meaning: The minimal root object is a retained distinction: a difference between two states not erased by the reader relevant to the current construction.

equations.section: III.A Retained distinction and graph structure
equations.text: L_R = D_W - W
equations.meaning: Weighted retained relations induce a graph-Laplacian-type operator, where W is the retained adjacency and D_W its weighted degree matrix.

equations.section: III.A Retained distinction and graph structure
equations.text: S_{n+1} = F(S_n, u_n, c_n, T_n)
equations.meaning: The root state evolves through a context-sensitive stepper, where u_n is an intervention/action, c_n is context, and T_n is the ordered/retained lineage tape.

equations.section: III.B Domain translation and reader equivalence
equations.text: q_D(F(z,u,c,T)) = F_D(q_D(z), u, c, T)
equations.meaning: An admissible domain quotient must preserve the root dynamics after translation.

equations.section: III.B Domain translation and reader equivalence
equations.text: O_D(z; Q, c) = O^#_D(q_D(z); Q, c)
equations.meaning: An admissible domain quotient must preserve required readouts within a declared horizon.

equations.section: III.B Domain translation and reader equivalence
equations.text: z ~_{Q,O,c,L} z'  <=>  O(F^k z) = O(F^k z')  for all k <= L
equations.meaning: Two internal descriptions are equivalent only relative to a question, reader, context, and horizon; this is a no-early-collapse rule preventing merger of states that could later be distinguished.

equations.text: retention -> structure -> translation -> readout -> meaning -> experience -> memory -> belief -> claim -> checking -> status -> public report
equations.meaning: States the mandatory order in which epistemic terms may be introduced; the forbidden order starts from a familiar name and retrospectively presents the result as knowledge.

equations.section: IV From occurrence to meaning, experience, and memory
equations.text: A != x != mu != E != M != Bel != p != sigma_K(p)
equations.meaning: Non-collapse law: occurrence, trace, meaning, experience, memory, belief, claim, and epistemic status of the claim are all typed-distinct objects.

equations.section: IV From occurrence to meaning, experience, and memory
equations.text: x_{i,n} = Access(A_n; O_i, L_i, T_i, R_i, C_i)
equations.meaning: An agency's accessible trace of an occurrence is mediated by reader, language, tool system, access rights, and context.

equations.section: IV From occurrence to meaning, experience, and memory
equations.text: A_i = A_j  =/=>  x_i = x_j
equations.meaning: Non-identity of traces under a shared occurrence is an access statement, not relativism: the same event can leave unequal readers with unequal resolution/vocabulary/permission/instrument.

equations.section: IV From occurrence to meaning, experience, and memory
equations.text: mu_{i,n} = G_mu(x_{i,n}, M_{i,n-1}, K_{i,n-1}, Theta_{i,n-1}, I_{i,n-1}, S_{i,n}^active, c_n)
equations.meaning: Meaning is generated downstream of the trace, as a function of trace, prior memory, prior knowledge state, prior identity/state, prior information, active state, and context.

equations.section: IV From occurrence to meaning, experience, and memory
equations.text: E_{i,n} = Phi_E(x_{i,n}, mu_{i,n}, kappa_{i,n}, c_n)
equations.meaning: Experience is a typed function of trace, meaning, an accessibility/control parameter kappa, and context (the MEMK-domain experience equation).

equations.section: IV From occurrence to meaning, experience, and memory
equations.text: M_{i,n} = U_M(M_{i,n-1}, x_{i,n}, mu_{i,n}, E_{i,n}, c_n, Lineage_n, T_n)
equations.meaning: Memory updates as a function of prior memory, current trace, meaning, experience, context, and lineage.

equations.section: IV From occurrence to meaning, experience, and memory
equations.text: Delta A_past = 0
equations.meaning: Historical-invariant law: the historical occurrence is not rewritten by later interpretation; reinterpretation changes bindings among trace/meaning/experience/memory while preserving the past occurrence.

equations.text: Bel_{i,p,n} = Rel_B(a_i, p | x_i, mu_i, E_i, M_i, Theta_i, I_i, S_i^active, c_i)
equations.meaning: Belief is not identical to a proposition; it is a conditioned relation between an agency and a proposition, given trace, meaning, experience, memory, identity/state, information, and context.
The canonical belief vector: endorsement, subjective confidence, salience, action readiness, identity binding, perceived social support, and resistance to revision.

equations.text: b_{i,p,n+1} = U_B(b_{i,p,n}, Ev_{i,p}, M_i, mu_i, E_i, Theta_i, I_i, Trust_i, Affect_i, Utility_i, Repetition_i, Auth_i, Pow_i, Access_i, Language_i, Algorithm_i, Obj_i, c_i)
equations.meaning: Belief formation combines epistemic and non-epistemic influences (descriptive, not justificatory): repetition, authority, power, incentives, identity, algorithms, and affect can strengthen a belief without increasing its epistemic validity.

equations.text: Bel_{g,d,n}^{(l)}(p) = Stabilize_B({b_{i,p,n}}_{i in G}, C_B)
equations.meaning: A locally shared belief is a stabilization of individual belief vectors across a group under communication/trust/practice/authority/lineage conditions C_B.

equations.text: Belief Strength(p), Belief Distribution(p), Auth(p), Pow(p), Val_E(p)
equations.meaning: Non-collapse separation: belief strength, belief distribution, authority, power, and epistemic validity of a claim are kept as distinct quantities (no truth ladder from scale).

equations.label: Prop-1
equations.text: Belief-scale nonpromotion: for any proposition p, increasing the distribution scale of Bel(p) does not, without additional gate information, increase sigma_K(p).
equations.meaning: Proved from Eq.(19): belief-update variables (repetition, visibility, sanctions, authority, algorithms) are not components of the knowledge-admission function, so distribution scale cannot be projected into epistemic status without a separate evidentiary bridge.

equations.label: Def-1
equations.text: Knowledge status: Knowledge is the bounded epistemic status granted to a claim about the world or a declared domain when the claim is produced and checked through an auditable process exposing agency, access, provenance, evidence, method, inference, assumptions, uncertainty, scope, objection, correction, independence, and lineage.
equations.meaning: Defines knowledge as an auditable status attached to a claim under stated conditions, not inherited from the speaker's identity or rank.

equations.text: sigma_K(p) = Admit_E(p | Agent, D, C, O, Access, Language, Tools, Rights, Prov, Ev, Method, Infer, Assumptions, Uncertainty, Scope, Obj, CorrCond, Independence, Lineage)
equations.meaning: Formal admission function producing the bounded epistemic status of a claim from the full set of typed gate inputs.

equations.text: K_p = <p, C_p, P_p, E_p, M_p, I_p, U_p, Omega_p, O_p, L_p, sigma_K(p)>
equations.meaning: The complete knowledge object is not merely the proposition p but a typed record grouping context/access, provenance, evidence, method, inference, uncertainty, scope, objections/correction, lineage, and status.

equations.section: VI.B Status of speaker and status of claim
equations.text: StatusOfSpeaker != StatusOfClaim;  Auth(p) != Val_E(p);  Pow(p) != Val_E(p)
equations.meaning: Non-collapse law: expertise, office, certification, citation count, or legal competence may affect priors/access/consequence but cannot close a claim's evidence and inference gates by themselves.

equations.section: VI.C Practical effectiveness as a separate axis
equations.text: Pi_prac(p) = TestPerformance(Y, Y_hat, intervention, C, O)
equations.meaning: Practical effectiveness of a claim is defined via outcome/prediction testing under intervention.

equations.section: VI.C Practical effectiveness as a separate axis
equations.text: sigma_K(p) != Pi_prac(p)
equations.meaning: Non-collapse law: epistemic status and practical/operational performance are distinct axes; a claim can have high status without being an effective intervention, and vice versa.

equations.text: chi_G in {1, 0, perp};  1 = ADMITTED, 0 = OBSTRUCTED, perp = UNRESOLVED
equations.meaning: Each of the thirteen admission gates (G0-G13) takes one of three values, preventing absence of evidence from being silently converted into success or failure.

equations.section: VII.B State sufficiency and invariant completion
equations.text: Suff_{E,L}(Z_E^cand; Q, O, c, T) in {1, 0, perp}
equations.meaning: A candidate domain state is audited for sufficiency (covering current readout, dynamics, intervention, delayed return, memory, coupling, geometry, basis, boundary) with a three-valued outcome.

equations.section: VII.B State sufficiency and invariant completion
equations.text: Inv_E(z) != Inv_E(z')  =>  q_E(z) != q_E(z')
equations.meaning: A quotient may not merge states that differ on a required future invariant; this is the epistemic form of candidate preservation.

equations.text: tau_public(p) <= inf_{g in G_p} tau(g)
equations.meaning: The strongest publicly assignable claim tier is bounded above by the weakest (infimum) tier licensed across all load-bearing gates for p.

equations.label: Prop-2
equations.text: Weakest-link claim ceiling: if any load-bearing gate for p is unresolved or obstructed, a public claim that presupposes that gate may not be assigned a stronger status than that gate.
equations.meaning: Proved from claim-identity and lineage requirements: a stronger public status would encode information not licensed by the conjunction of gate records, so would not be reconstructible from the auditable inputs.

equations.text: sigma_K(p) in {ADMITTED, LOCAL, TRANSPORTABLE, UNRESOLVED, OBSTRUCTED, RETRACTED, SUPERSEDED}
equations.meaning: The full status space for a claim's epistemic status, where retraction and supersession preserve lineage and reasons for change (not erasure).

equations.section: VIII Local, institutional, and global knowledge
equations.text: Omega(K) = {(g, d, l, P, O, c) : all required gates pass}
equations.meaning: Knowledge scope is defined as the set of gate/domain/local-scope/practice/observer/context tuples for which all required gates pass.

equations.section: VIII Local, institutional, and global knowledge
equations.text: K_local = K |_{Omega_local}
equations.meaning: Local knowledge is the restriction of the full knowledge object to the local scope.

equations.section: VIII Local, institutional, and global knowledge
equations.text: T^Y_{ij} o K_i ~= K_j o T^C_{ij};  epsilon_bridge = d(T^Y_{ij} o K_i, K_j o T^C_{ij})
equations.meaning: A global claim requires a declared, tolerance-bounded transport (commuting-square) relation between contexts i and j before local knowledge can be presented as global.

equations.section: VIII Local, institutional, and global knowledge
equations.text: Bel_global(p) != K_global(p)
equations.meaning: Non-collapse law: a widely distributed/stabilized belief is not the same as globally transported knowledge, regardless of media selection, accreditation, political power, or algorithmic amplification behind the belief's scale.

equations.section: IX.A Agency as a process quotient
equations.text: A_{i,n} = q_A(Z_{i,n}; Q_A, O_A, c_n)
equations.meaning: The epistemic agent is a query-relative quotient of a retained state, not an indivisible substance.

equations.section: IX.A Agency as a process quotient
equations.text: Aut(F_A, O_A) = {h : O_A o h = O_A, h o F_A = F_A o h}
equations.meaning: Two internal self-descriptions count as the same operational agent when all required future readouts agree; this automorphism class formalizes that gauge-like redundancy.

equations.section: IX.A Agency as a process quotient
equations.text: I_n = q_comp(M_n (+) Bel_n (+) Theta_n (+) Roles_n (+) BodyTool_n (+) SocialLineage_n)
equations.meaning: Identity is compositional: a typed quotient over memory, belief, identity-state, roles, embodiment/tools, and social lineage (direct-sum notation is typed, not numeric addition).

equations.text: x_n -> zeta_n -> v_n -> rho_n -> U_n -> beta_n -> I_{n+1} -> a_n -> S_{n+1}
equations.meaning: The continuous chain between readout and renewed state: contact, valence, drive, identity binding, appropriated experience, action, and renewed state.

equations.text: zeta_n = Contact(x_n, O_n, BodyTool_n, Attention_n, c_n)
equations.meaning: Contact is a function of trace, reader, embodiment/tools, attention, and context.

equations.text: v_n = V_valence(zeta_n, M_n, mu_n, BodyState_n, c_n)
equations.meaning: Valence is a function of contact, memory, meaning, body state, and context.

equations.text: rho_n = R_drive(v_n, ExpectedRelief_n, ExpectedGain_n, Habit_n, c_n)
equations.meaning: Drive is a function of valence, expected relief, expected gain, habit, and context.

equations.text: U_n = Bind_self(rho_n, Bel_n, Theta_n, I_n, S_n^active, c_n)
equations.meaning: Identity binding is a function of drive, belief, identity-state, identity, active state, and context.

equations.text: xi_n = (xi_n^+, xi_n^-, xi_n^0)
equations.meaning: The distortion vector: approach amplification, aversive rejection, and model-blindness components.

equations.text: Xi_n = alpha_n^+ P_n^+ + alpha_n^- P_n^- + alpha_n^0 P_n^0;  G~_{mu,n} = G_{mu,n} o (I + Xi_n)
equations.meaning: The meaning operator is distorted by a weighted combination of approach/aversion/blindness projections.

equations.text: epsilon_{Xi,n} = d_O(G_{mu,n}(z_n), G~_{mu,n}(z_n))
equations.meaning: The distortion defect measures the readout-space distance between undistorted and distorted meaning; identity protection/attraction/aversion/ignorance can alter meaning without increasing epistemic status.

equations.text: S_A[n] = q_self(F^n[delta_R, T_A, c_{0:n}]) = <A_A[n], Delta_A[n], H_A[n], Phen_A^str[n], P_A^lived[n], Own_A[n], Coh_A[n], Val_A[n], Pi_A[n], Lambda_A[n]>_~self
equations.meaning: The complete self object is a typed quotient bundling agency, identity change, horizon state, structural phenomenality, lived phenomenality, ownership, coherence, valence, policy, and lineage.

equations.text: A_A != I_A != Phen_A^str != P_A^lived != Own_A != Coh_A != Val_A
equations.meaning: Non-collapse law: agency, identity, structural phenomenality, lived phenomenality, ownership, coherence, and valence remain dissociable readout lanes of one root.

equations.text: I_A[n+1] = q_id(I_A[n] (+) A_A[n] (+) P_A^lived[n] (+) Pi_A^star[n] (+) Res_A[n] (+) Delta T_A[n])
equations.meaning: Identity update: identity is agency continued through append-only typed lineage composition; a one-time action is not yet a self.

equations.text: H_dyn: Delta_A(lambda) = D_A^2 - 4 M_A K_A lambda = 0
equations.meaning: The dynamical horizon is defined as the discriminant threshold of a characteristic quadratic form.

equations.text: H_info(A) = {z in Z_A : Rec(z) => (E_b < infinity, R_p > 0)}
equations.meaning: The information horizon is the boundary beyond which no admissible external inverse path recovers the internal state without bounded emission.

equations.text: H_phen(A) = {r = A_A^acc Pi_A T_A(delta_R) : PhenGate(r) = 1}
equations.meaning: The phenomenal horizon contains self-indexed, embodied, owned, coherent, and action-consequential records passing the phenomenal gate.

equations.text: H_dyn --DI_K--> H_info --IP_K--> H_phen
equations.meaning: The proposed weld linking the dynamical, information, and phenomenal horizons; only the threshold and information-horizon structures are conditionally derived, the sufficiency bridge IP_K remains open.

equations.text: Phen_A^str[n] = A_A^acc Pi_A T_A^{<=n}(delta_R; T_A, c_n)
equations.meaning: Structural phenomenality is a bounded, accessible, projected transform of the retained-distinction history up to step n.

equations.text: P_A^lived[n] = Phi_A^phen(M_A^rec[n], Omega_A[n], B_A[n], c_n)
equations.meaning: A lived event is a further bounded transformation of recorded memory, an omega-state, a body state, and context; the framework does not infer subjective consciousness from accessibility alone.

equations.text: K_prop(p) = sigma_K(p)
equations.meaning: Ordinary propositional knowledge is identified with the bounded epistemic status of the claim.

equations.text: K_op(p) = <K_prop(p), Task_p, Completion_p>
equations.meaning: Operational knowledge adds a task and an independent completion certificate to propositional knowledge.

equations.text: K_trans(p) = <K_op(p), Delta Theta, Delta I, Delta U, Delta Action, Persistence, Transport, Viability>
equations.meaning: Transformative knowledge adds persistent changes in view, identity, binding, action, context transport, and viability; mandatory only when a claim asserts that a practice changes the knower.

equations.text: sigma_K(p) = ADMITTED
equations.meaning: First required condition for an admitted transformation: the underlying claim must itself be admitted.

equations.text: Completion_p = PASS
equations.meaning: Second required condition for an admitted transformation: the task completion certificate must pass.

equations.text: z_post in V_A
equations.meaning: Third required condition: the post-transformation state must lie in the viability set.

equations.text: Defects_{persistence, transport, lineage} <= tau
equations.meaning: Fourth required condition: persistence, transport, and lineage defects must be bounded by a tolerance; intensity/conviction/surprise/life-change are not substitutes for these conditions.

equations.text: U_{n+1} = Pi_{U>=0}[(I - D_U) U_n + J_{reinforce,n} - J_{release,n}]
equations.meaning: The identity-binding update under reinforcement and release forcing, projected onto nonnegative values.

equations.text: J_release - J_reinforce >= epsilon_release > 0
equations.meaning: A sufficient conditional release criterion: persistent dominance of release over reinforcement.
Release additionally requires viability and continuing nonzero readout while the binding norm decays to zero; release is not death, memory deletion, passivity, or loss of causal agency.

equations.text: v_free in ker B_I,  B_I v_free = 0,  O_E(v_free) != 0
equations.meaning: A nonbinding mode: content in the kernel of the binding operator remains readable while no longer functioning as an identity necessity.
Current-state readout: a first-order reader applied to the agency quotient of the retained state.
Meta-readout is reader composition: a readout of the current-state readout.
The meta-readout is retained over a finite window (finite retention).

equations.section: XII.B Interruptibility, alternatives, and policy revision
equations.text: R_A^{(1)} != Claim_A != Identity_A;  Identity_A != ActionCandidate_A != CommittedAction_A
equations.meaning: Non-collapse law (typed-state decoupling): current readout, claim, identity, action candidate, and committed action remain distinct, preventing a transient readout from becoming a claim/identity/command merely because it is salient.

equations.section: XII.B Interruptibility, alternatives, and policy revision
equations.text: C_A^ret[n] = O_A^ctx(c_{n-h:n}, T_{n-h:n})
equations.meaning: Context access: a readout over a finite window of recent context and lineage.

equations.section: XII.B Interruptibility, alternatives, and policy revision
equations.text: L_A^acc[n] = O_A^lin(Lambda_A[n], T_n)
equations.meaning: Lineage access: a readout over the lineage record.

equations.section: XII.B Interruptibility, alternatives, and policy revision
equations.text: U_A[n] = {u : C_A(u | Z_A[n], c_n, T_n) = 1}
equations.meaning: The admissible candidate-action set given the current admissibility condition.

equations.section: XII.B Interruptibility, alternatives, and policy revision
equations.text: F_A^act[n] = O_A^act(U_A[n], Pi_A[n])
equations.meaning: Action formation is exposed as a readout over the admissible candidate set and current policy.

equations.section: XII.B Interruptibility, alternatives, and policy revision
equations.text: I_A^resp[n] = 1  <=>  exists u' != u*: u' in U_A[n], t < t_c, Repair(F(Z_A, u')) >= R_min
equations.meaning: Response interruptibility at commitment time t_c: an alternative action exists before commitment that would achieve sufficient repair.

equations.section: XII.B Interruptibility, alternatives, and policy revision
equations.text: A_A^pol[n] = O_A^alt(U_A[n])
equations.meaning: Alternative-policy access: a readout exposing the alternative-action landscape.

equations.section: XII.B Interruptibility, alternatives, and policy revision
equations.text: Pi_A^star[n] = arg min_{u in U_A[n]} J_A(u)
equations.meaning: Policy reconfiguration selects the admissible action minimizing the governance cost functional.

equations.section: XII.B Interruptibility, alternatives, and policy revision
equations.text: J_A(u) = E||Res_{A,u}||^2 + lambda_C C(u) + rho R(u) + mu L_repair(u) - nu V(u)
equations.meaning: The governance cost functional combining expected residual, a constraint cost, a regularizer, a repair-loss term, and a viability reward; weights are target-domain parameters, not root constants.

equations.section: XII.B Interruptibility, alternatives, and policy revision
equations.text: u_A^repair = arg min_{u in U_A^repair} (||Res_A(F(Z_A,u))||^2 + Cost(u) + RepairLoss(u))
equations.meaning: Residual-guided repair in discrete form: the admissible action minimizing residual, cost, and repair loss; a gradient approximation requires an independently supplied differentiable local encoding.

equations.text: G_A^MR[n] = <R_A^{(1)}, R_A^{(2)}, W_A^R, D_A^type, C_A^ret, L_A^acc, F_A^act, I_A^resp, A_A^pol, Pi_A^star, Delta Z_A^repair>_n
equations.meaning: The full governance state bundles current readout, meta-readout, finite retention, typed decoupling, context/lineage access, action formation, interruptibility, alternative-policy access, policy, and repair residual.

equations.text: G_A^MR[n] = R_{tau_g}(O_A(O_A(q_A(Z_A[n]))), C_A^ret, L_A^acc, F_A, Pi_A)
equations.meaning: A compact operator computing the governance state from readout-of-readout composition, context/lineage access, action formation, and policy.

equations.text: Delta_G Pi_A^star = d_Pi(Pi_A^star, Pi_{A,-G}^star) > tau_idle
equations.meaning: The operator is governance-relevant only when ablating a component G changes the resulting policy (or an analogous repair distance exceeds tolerance) beyond an idle threshold.

equations.section: XII.D Defect vector, capture, and finite self-readout
equations.text: epsilon_G = (epsilon_R1, epsilon_R2, epsilon_W, epsilon_D, epsilon_C, epsilon_L, epsilon_F, epsilon_I, epsilon_A, epsilon_Pi, epsilon_repair)
equations.meaning: The primary governance diagnostic is a typed defect vector; a summary norm may not replace it since different defects require different repairs.

equations.section: XII.D Defect vector, capture, and finite self-readout
equations.text: Gamma_A = Load_A - Capacity_A
equations.meaning: The conditional capture margin; if it exceeds a threshold, governance capture becomes a live diagnostic candidate (weights/threshold uncalibrated).

equations.section: XII.D Defect vector, capture, and finite self-readout
equations.text: CurrentReadout + SelectionPriority + SelectionStability + SelfReport  =/=>  G_A^MR
equations.meaning: The no-free-governance law: a stable selected channel, selection priority/stability, and self-report do not jointly imply full governance; lost context, missing alternatives, opaque action formation, and unavailable repair can still coexist.

equations.section: XII.D Defect vector, capture, and finite self-readout
equations.text: B_G = I(R_A^{(2)}; Z_A) / tau_cA < infinity,  ker O_A^{(2)} != empty
equations.meaning: For a bounded agency with a sufficiently rich state, mutual information between meta-readout and retained state is bounded and the meta-readout operator has nontrivial kernel; the architecture rejects complete self-transparency and exact zero empirical governance defect.

equations.section: XIII Human-AI relation and knowledge civilization
equations.text: AIOutput != ClaimIdentity != Evidence;  Evidence != Inference != KnowledgeStatus
equations.meaning: Non-collapse law: an AI output's generative capability does not by itself grant automatic knowledge status; the typed separations among output, claim identity, evidence, inference, and status must hold.

equations.section: XIII Human-AI relation and knowledge civilization
equations.text: T_{H<-AI} o K_AI ~= K_H o T_C
equations.meaning: A bounded transport relation is required between AI-produced and human-produced knowledge objects, with explicit defects for semantic loss, source omission, authority laundering, uncertainty compression, and context mismatch.
